reconcile.note: Fausset and his co-authors tie Paul's wish for tongues in 1 Corinthians 14:5 to intelligible languages, not the unintelligible noise 14:8-9 condemns.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible reads 1 Corinthians 14:2-5's endorsement of tongues as flatly opposed to the trumpet-noise ridicule of unintelligible speech in 14:8-9.

sides.snippet: Now I desire to have you all speak with other languages, but rather that you would prophesy.
sides.verseText: Now I desire to have you all speak with other languages, but rather that you would prophesy. For he is greater who prophesies than he who speaks with other languages, unless he interprets, that the assembly may be built up.

sides.snippet: So also you, unless you uttered by the tongue words easy to understand, how would it be known what is spoken?
sides.verseText: So also you, unless you uttered by the tongue words easy to understand, how would it be known what is spoken? For you would be speaking into the air.
